{{short description|British physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}}
'''Alexander (Alec) Boksenberg''' [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 18 March 1936)<ref>{{Citation
 | title = Birthdays
 | newspaper = [[The Guardian]]
 | pages = 35
 | date = 17 March 2014
 }}</ref> is a British scientist who was the [[Director of the Royal Greenwich Observatory]] from 1981–1995. In the early 1980s he developed the [[image photon counting system]], an electronic detector for faint astronomical sources.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boksenberg |first1=Alexander |title=Advances in detectors for astronomical spectroscopy |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences |date=12 November 1982 |volume=307 |issue=1500 |pages=531–548 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1982.0128|bibcode=1982RSPTA.307..531B }}</ref> His astronomical research focused on [[active galactic nuclei]].

Boksenberg won the 1998 [[Jackson-Gwilt Medal]] from the [[Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=D. |date=1998-08-01 |title=Prof. Alec Boksenberg, CBE, FRS: Jackson Gwilt Medal |url=https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/astrog/39.4.4.7-a |journal=Astronomy & Geophysics |language=en |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=4.7–a–4.7 |doi=10.1093/astrog/39.4.4.7-a |issn=1366-8781|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the 1999 [[Hughes Medal]] from the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/annualreport/1996-7/h.html |title=Annual Report: Awards & Prizes
|publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]|access-date=2009-02-07|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060105025632/http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/annualreport/1996-7/h.html |archive-date = 2006-01-05}}</ref> The minor planet [[3205 Boksenberg]] is named after him.<ref>{{cite book|title=(3205) Boksenberg In: Dictionary of Minor Planet Names |publisher=Springer |date=2003 |isbn=978-3-540-29925-7 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-29925-7_3206}}</ref>

He won the [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize]] in 2000.{{cn|date=May 2024}}
